questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Laos?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Laos on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Laos article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Myanmar and by China to the northwest, by Vietnam to the east, by Cambodia to the south and by Thailand to the west.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Laos?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Laos article.

questions.proof: Boats from Laos cannot get to the ocean using the Mekong because of rapids and waterfalls in the south of the country.[5] Laos is the least densely populated country in Southeast Asia, with 32 people per square kilometer.[6] A railway connection between Thailand and Laos has been operational since July 2024, with trains running to Khamsavath railway station in Vientiane prefecture.[7]

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Vientiane?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Laos is Vientiane.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Laos about 236,800 square kilometres; Nepal about 147,181 square kilometres; Estonia about 45,335 square kilometres; Taiwan about 36,197 square kilometres.
